transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello. My moods have been all over the place lately, and I feel wound up and irritated with everyone at home. My husband and my pastor actually persuaded me to come to the clinic today because they are worried about me.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt abnormally high or energetic, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were risky or out of character?

Yes, that is exactly what has been happening for about a month now. I feel like a "super-umma" on top of the world, waking up at 3 a.m. buzzing with energy to clean or prep food after only a few hours of sleep. I've also been talking so fast my family tells me to slow down, and spending money we don't really have on bulk food and art supplies for my big plans.
Have you ever had a separate period of depression lasting at least two weeks, with low mood or loss of interest, especially before or after this elevated period?
No, I don't recall ever having a period of deep depression or losing interest in things like that. My main struggle has really just been how wound up and irritated I've been feeling lately.

Have these symptoms caused major problems at work, at home, or with money, or led to a need for hospitalization? Also, have you had any hallucinations or beliefs that others said were clearly not true?

Yes, it’s caused a lot of trouble because I’m making mistakes and leaving tasks unfinished at the warehouse, constantly arguing with my family, and spending money we don't really have on bulk food and art supplies. I haven't needed to go to the hospital, though, and I definitely haven't had any hallucinations or unusual beliefs.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a clear manic syndrome lasting about 1 month with elevated/expansive mood, markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, pressured/rapid speech, increased goal-directed activity, irritability, and excessive spending. Symptoms caused clear functional impairment at work and home, but there is no history of a major depressive episode and no psychotic symptoms or hospitalization, supporting a manic episode rather than bipolar disorder or psychotic disorder.
